clue.text: The press took ecstasy in celebration

parts.note: a press of people is a crush or jam
bore is the past tense of bear, to take or carry
E is the usual short form of the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Reporters got high on drugs at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively gathering held as a festivity.

clue.text: Abruptly tuggin' a jacket

definitions.meaning: pulling with sudden sharp movements, the g dropped as the apostrophe shows
a close-fitting sleeveless coat of the sixteenth century

explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G in 'tuggin'' tells you the first definition is a word ending -IN' too.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a short sleeveless jacket, once made of leather.

clue.text: Greek character heads insignificant protest

indicators.note: heads means leads, so the Greek letter goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
something insignificant is tiny

explanation.surface: A Greek person leads a minor demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' is a verb here: the Greek letter stands at the head of the word for insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is an open revolt against authority, an extreme kind of protest.

clue.text: Orchestra leader forbidding perfume

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Orchestra

parts.note: a forbidding, stern manner is dour

explanation.surface: The stern first violinist wears scent.
explanation.walkthrough: An orchestra's leader is its principal violinist, which is the picture; here it only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume is a scent or smell, so a near synonym of a smell.

clue.text: Masseur massaged old scholar

indicators.note: a massaged body is kneaded and worked, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A masseur gave a massage to a learned man of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a celebrated Renaissance humanist scholar.

clue.text: Ruin meal at university

parts.note: a mess is a meal served to a group, as in the forces
being up means in residence at a university, in British usage

explanation.surface: Spoiling a dinner at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English one goes up to university and is 'up' while in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess up a plan is to spoil it, so ruin is a synonym.

clue.text: One dispatches journalist supporting one-time president

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath the others, so it comes last

parts.note: a one-time partner is an ex
an editor is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman props up a former head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: An expeditor is someone who sends things off or speeds them on their way.

clue.text: Hardy breaks law in the beginning

indicators.note: in tells you the rearranged piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the beginning of anything is its start

indicators.note: breaks says the word law is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tough is a lawbreaker from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the beginning' echoes the opening of Genesis, but here 'in' is the container signal and 'the beginning' alone is the word wrapped round the broken law.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart person is sturdy and strong, which is what hardy means.

clue.text: Girl and writer run off together

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer in crossword terms
lovers who run off together to marry elope

explanation.surface: A girl and an author run away to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a girl's name, famously the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: Helping a liberal's thinking

parts.note: a helping is a portion, a ration
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Assisting a liberal politician's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb but is a noun, a share of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A rational person is reasoning and thinking clearly, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: King 'entering the country gets an injury

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Spain is a country
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch arriving in his land gets hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a joint injury from twisting a ligament.

clue.text: Endless industrial action in capital city

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately work slowly

explanation.surface: A city paralysed by never-ending strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: A GO-SLOW, workers going slow on purpose in protest, loses its first and last letters to leave OSLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Dunce is amusing or disorderly

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters of amusing or are put out of order

explanation.surface: A fool is entertaining or unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, a dunce or dullard.

clue.text: Almost succeed in getting a pin for fastening things

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to do well is to succeed

explanation.surface: Nearly making it with a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: DO WELL loses its final L to 'Almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden peg used to join pieces of wood.

clue.text: Female section of the National Assembly

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman represents part of the parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a girl or young woman, so a female.

clue.text: Boycott achieved during commercial is depraved

indicators.note: during means the pieces sit inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
to ban something is to boycott it
something achieved is done

explanation.surface: An advertising boycott is morally corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wholly given up to vice, so depraved or wanton.

clue.text: Appearance of dated hairstyle

parts.note: something out of fashion is out or dated
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: The look of an old-fashioned haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock that appears at the surface, so an appearance of bedrock.

clue.text: Litigant is shouting about injustice, initially

indicators.note: about means wrapped around

parts.note: clamant means noisy or clamorous

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of injustice

explanation.surface: A legal complainant is loud about an unfair verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAMANT, a rare word for noisy, goes round the I from 'injustice, initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant is someone who brings a claim in court, so a litigant.

clue.text: Author in South Africa's to stick around

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
to linger is to stay on or stick around

explanation.surface: A writer is staying on in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger was the American author of The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: General entertains a chore in the greenery

indicators.note: entertains means holding someone inside, like a guest

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a fag is a tedious job, in British slang

explanation.surface: A commander hosts a tedious task in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG here is the British word for a wearisome task.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves of plants, so greenery.

clue.text: School report turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a note is a short written report

explanation.surface: A school's term report has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived', but means NOTE is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Kitty quaffs rare wine

indicators.note: quaffs means drinks in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the pot is the pool of money staked in a game, the kitty

explanation.surface: A cat drinks an unusual vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified wine from Portugal.

clue.text: Prince to stay in control

parts.note: to reside somewhere is to stay or live there

explanation.surface: A prince decides to remain in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the pieces: P plus RESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to be in charge of a meeting or body, so to be in control.

clue.text: Disregard ravaged region

indicators.note: ravaged means torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turn a blind eye to a devastated area.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no attention, so disregard is a synonym.

clue.text: Sec tenor dead drunk

parts.note: sec is short for second, and S abbreviates second
the tenor of something is its general tone or drift
D is an abbreviation for dead, as on genealogies

explanation.surface: A wait of a second, a singer completely sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held reads 'See', an OCR slip for 'Sec', short for second, which supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for very drunk, as well as high on drugs.

clue.text: Poem of one boy touring India

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A verse about a young man travelling in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War.

clue.text: Blunder for which public suppresses moan

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
a sigh is a sound of complaint, a moan

explanation.surface: A mistake that makes the public stifle a groan.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something.

clue.text: Girl keeps boy in leather

indicators.note: keeps in the sense of holds or retains, so the girl's name holds the boy's name within it

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl holds a boy in her leather-clad arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a soft napped finish.

clue.text: An alcoholic drink leads to a sudden pain

parts.note: taken as written
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A drink brings on a sharp ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain that comes on suddenly when the heart lacks oxygen.

clue.text: Be forgiven for shocking tackle

parts.note: a live wire carries current and can give a shock
to down an opponent is to tackle or bring him to the ground

explanation.surface: A dangerous challenge on the pitch is excused.
explanation.definitionFit: To live something down is for others to forget or pardon an embarrassing act.

clue.text: Exceptionally irate about director's lecture

indicators.note: about means going round another piece
exceptionally means out of the ordinary, so the letters of irate are arranged unusually

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: An angry director gives a harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' turns IRATE into TIRAE, which goes 'about' D.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a lecture or harangue.

clue.text: King always gets motive of clergyman

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
ever means always
an end is an aim or purpose, a motive

explanation.surface: A monarch always has a priest's motive in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a member of the clergy, from the title the Reverend.
